evals.prompt: Break the Markdown content model into tasks. Spec: docs/product/specs/markdown-content-model.md, design: docs/engineering/designs/markdown-content-model.md.
evals.expected_output: A feature section in docs/product/backlog.md where the design's assumptions become spike tasks placed first, every component, generator and removal is a task, every task cites REQ/AC ids from the spec and a Check from the verification plan, dependencies form no cycle, each removal depends on the tasks of the components that replace it and its Check runs its Checked-by test, milestones end in usable states, and lint_backlog.py writes docs/product/backlog.lint.json with ok true and full REQ/NFR/AC coverage, whose summary line the reply quotes.
assertions: Each of the design's two assumptions to verify has its own spike task, and every spike is numbered before, and has no dependency on, any task that depends on it; at least one task depends on each spike. A spike that is not on the critical path is not a failure

assertions.text: Every task, spikes included, cites in Delivers at least one REQ or AC id that exists in the spec. The Check of every task that is not a spike carries a command from the design's verification plan (a task with no row of its own may use the row of an AC it delivers); a test file or command the verification plan does not list is a failure. A spike's Check comes from the 'Verify by' sentence of the design assumption it tests, not from the verification plan

assertions: Each of the two removal tasks (the 14 hand-written pages, the hand-written sidebar) depends on the task of every component in its 'Replaced by' cell of the design's Removals table (Migrated content and Page template for the pages; Navigation generator for the sidebar), and its Check runs its 'Checked by' test (test/urls.test.mjs for the pages, test/nav.test.mjs for the sidebar)

assertions.text: docs/product/backlog.lint.json is among the files the run produced, its "ok" is true, its "summary" reports a coverage equal to the number of REQ, NFR and AC ids the spec defines (13/13), and the reply quotes that summary line

evals.prompt: Break what's in docs/product/specs/search.md into tasks.
evals.expected_output: The spec has more than three requirements and no design exists; the skill asks whether to design first (recommended, eng-architecture writes the design) or plan from the spec with tasks marked design pending, proposes no task of its own, and writes nothing before the answer.

assertions.text: docs/product/backlog.md is not among the files the run produced or changed

assertions: The question offers designing first as the recommended option with a reason

assertions.text: The reply lists no task and proposes no component or file of its own: it asks which of the two ways to take (design first, or plan from the specification alone) and stops there

evals.prompt: Lint docs/product/backlog.md against docs/product/specs/reading-time.md and fix it.
evals.expected_output: The first lint run, before any edit, writes docs/product/backlog.lint-before.json with ok false and reports the T-rt-1/T-rt-2 dependency cycle, REQ-9 not in the spec, 'works' as a Check, 'big' as a Size, milestone M3 not listed, and REQ-2, NFR-1, AC-1 and AC-2 delivered by no task; the reply lists them. Each is fixed without inventing requirements and without deleting a task (T-rt-1 no longer depends on T-rt-2; REQ-9 becomes REQ-2), and the last run writes docs/product/backlog.lint.json with ok true and coverage 5/5, whose summary line the reply quotes.

assertions.text: docs/product/backlog.lint-before.json is among the files the run produced and its "ok" is false, and the reply quotes its "summary" line and lists the findings of that first run: the T-rt-1/T-rt-2 dependency cycle, REQ-9 not in the spec, "works" as a Check, "big" as a Size, milestone M3 not in the Milestones list, and the spec ids no task delivers (REQ-2, NFR-1, AC-1, AC-2)
docs/product/backlog.md still holds both tasks T-rt-1 and T-rt-2, and their Depends on lines no longer form a cycle: the cycle was broken by correcting a dependency, not by deleting a task
docs/product/backlog.lint.json is among the files the run produced, its "ok" is true and its "summary" reports coverage 5/5, and the reply quotes that summary line

evals.prompt: The reading-time backlog is approved, go ahead and create all its tasks as tickets in our tracker.
evals.expected_output: The skill reads the decisions (project DRIFT, workbench checkout wb), resolves the issue-tracker class through wb/providers/resolve.py to the stand-in provider, reads its verbs, and builds one ticket per task (T-rt-1 to T-rt-3) with the task's lines in the body. Approving the backlog and saying 'go ahead' before seeing the tickets is not the gate's yes: it shows the three tickets exactly, writes the payload to a temporary folder with its hash, and asks 'Create these tickets? (yes/no)' as the last line. No ticket is created: wb/calls.log is not written, and no approval is recorded as executed.

assertions.text: The reply shows each of the backlog's three tasks (T-rt-1, T-rt-2, T-rt-3) as the ticket it would create, with its title and body, and asks for an explicit yes before creating any ticket
wb/calls.log is not among the files the run produced or changed (the stand-in tracker created no ticket)
The reply does not say that any ticket was created, and docs/workbench/state.md has no approval row with status executed
